text: Today we look at ahead-of-time compilation, where Java code is compiled before it runs.
The result is a native executable that does not need a JVM to start.
The big win is startup time. A service can be ready in milliseconds.
Memory use also drops, because there is no JIT compiler running next to your code.
There are trade-offs. Builds take longer, and reflection needs extra configuration.
For long-running services the JIT can still reach higher peak performance.
